summary: Preinstall dropper downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is written with obfuscator.io-style hex-prefixed identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and dispatch objects that indirect every string and call. Its behavior is to probe for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, download the Bun runtime v1.3.13 as a zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a tmp directory, extract it, chmod it executable (mode 493 / 0755), and invoke it on the shipped `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB file marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` containing a string-array cipher (`WV8StW` array-rotation, mixed-int/string table `n7gIxM`, decoder `hc1jfK9`) with no library exports; it is not referenced by the package's `main`/`module` entry (`lib/component.js`) and is unrelated to the package's advertised purpose (a Vue copyable-text UI component). The only path that reaches this file is the preinstall Bun-dispatch, which fires automatically on `npm install`. Executing an obfuscated ~700 KB payload under an alternate runtime at install time gives the author arbitrary code execution on the installer's host, and the alternate-runtime dispatch bypasses scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code paths.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
